prompt: Shuffle only a sub-range of an array with a seeded Fisher-Yates pass, leaving the values outside the range -- and the caller's original array -- untouched. Complete the shuffleRange method in the starter file.
explanation: Fisher-Yates walks backwards from the last slot, swapping each position with a randomly chosen one at or before it. Restricting it to [from, to) just means offsetting the random index by from and bounding the draw with (i - from + 1). Copying the source with Arrays.copyOf first keeps the method free of side effects, and a range of length 0 or 1 naturally draws no random numbers because the loop body never runs.
hints: Start with int[] copy = java.util.Arrays.copyOf(source, source.length) so the caller's array is safe.
Loop i from to - 1 down to from + 1; the random partner is from + rng.nextInt(i - from + 1).
Swapping needs a temporary variable: save copy[i], overwrite it with copy[j], then put the saved value into copy[j].
